source.title: On the benefits of non-linear weight updates

record.file_problem: The text contains the full paper and appendices, but Table 7 is referenced and its results are missing from the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: It compares held-out performance across standard and adaptive optimizers using a different benchmark and tuning procedure from the cited optimizer studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy or loss for standard optimizers, Adam, and proposed non-linear variants. Rows below retain SGD, Momentum, and Adam results relevant to V4; proposed non-linear variants and other optimizers are outside that version. The text gives no numeric results for Table 7.
record.test_reason: The study benchmarks its proposed nonlinear optimizers. Section 5 explicitly says the standard SGD, Momentum, NAG and Adam results are extracted from reference [16], so the recorded comparisons are cited results, not this study's own test of V4. Its own nonlinear-optimizer results do not establish any other claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct: nonlinear updates usually improve performance over corresponding conventional optimizers, especially on image classification, with exceptions including Quadratic Deep and Tolstoi momentum variants. The authors interpret this as suggestive evidence for their SNR-inspired approach, not a proof.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes nonlinear gradient transformations and compares them with standard optimizers in DeepOBS tasks; its medium hyperparameter randomization uses 50 samples per optimizer, selects by validation performance, and repeats the selected setting 10 times.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies across task and optimizer; the paper reports that NL-Momentum and NL-NAG underperform their conventional equivalents on Tolstoi, while Adam outperforms SGD and Momentum on MNIST VAE and Tolstoi.

fits_no_version.finding: The study's own nonlinear gradient transformations generally improve benchmark performance over imported conventional-optimizer baselines, with exceptions for Quadratic Deep and some Tolstoi variants.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Nonlinear transformations of gradient components can improve held-out performance relative to corresponding conventional optimizer implementations.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing dropout and repeating the search gives NL-NAG Tolstoi accuracy of 61.97, versus 61.57 ± 0.07 in its reported dropout configuration. This is a character-prediction model and the comparison also changes selected hyperparameters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout and optimizer tuning can affect the stability and accuracy of nonlinear-gradient character-prediction models.

record.problems: The study evaluates benchmark test accuracy/loss rather than explicitly analyzing training-test error gaps. The supplied text omits Table 7 results. The authors state that they do not formally prove their optimizer adaptations; parameter selection uses a medium random search and fixed momentum value.
record.rows_left_out: Proposed NL-SGD, NL-Mom, and NL-NAG results, NAG results, best-optimizer results, and additional annihilation-phase results were omitted because they do not directly compare Adam against SGD or Momentum for V4. Table 7 is absent from the supplied text.

untested.parts: Generalization as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Own-result comparisons of standard adaptive optimizers against SGD or momentum SGD, including tuning, training-performance and recovery conditions.
Controlled batch-size comparisons and recipe adaptations.
Controlled dropout effects in the specified classifier regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Table 7 is present. The two-column text interleaves its F-MNIST VAE losses with the Tolstoi section; Table 8 reports Tolstoi accuracy. Consequently, the record's missing-table assertion and Tolstoi loss comparisons are incorrect. All recorded standard-optimizer values are explicitly imported from [16], precluding verdicts based on them as independent results of this study.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Broader tuning beyond the paper's medium random search; decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, and comparisons outside the listed benchmark tasks.
Large-batch versus small-batch training under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Controlled dropout comparisons, including small-data and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.
